Yes—under those conditions, you’d very likely be able to spot the Moon.

- It is **48.3° above the horizon**, which is high in the sky.
- At **89.5% illumination**, it is nearly full and therefore very bright.
- The sky is only in **nautical twilight**; although the Sun is still 10.4° below the horizon, the sky is brighter than during full darkness, but a nearly full Moon should remain conspicuous.
- Its azimuth of **271.8°** places it almost due west, so look high toward the western sky.
- Clear conditions and normal unaided vision are more than sufficient.

The Moon may be somewhat less striking than it would be in a dark night sky, and nearby buildings, hills, trees, haze, or light pollution could interfere. But astronomically, it is absolutely not impossible to see—in fact, it should be easy to find if you look roughly west and high overhead.
